data.title:
You generated the draft.
Now it needs a person
paragraphs: A model will give you a clean page, and it will give everyone else the same one. The sentences restate each other in different words, the same few constructions carry every paragraph, and none of it is wrong, which is what makes it hard to argue with and easy to skip.

We edit AI-written content the way we write it. A human editor cuts the padding and the borrowed phrasing, then puts in a position worth holding, a detail nobody else has, and a sentence somebody would quote.

data.title: What is human editing for AI content?

items.label: What we do
items.value: You send content a model generated. A human editor rewrites it so it carries a position, real specifics, and your voice, and so an answer engine has a reason to quote it. People do the editing, so there is nothing to install and no prompt pack to learn.

items.label: Best for
items.value: Teams already publishing AI-generated content who can see it is not earning anything. Marketing leads producing more pages than one person can read. Companies whose library grew fast and reads like everyone else's.

items.label: Not for
items.value: Anyone looking for software to edit with. A tool that cleans up prose automatically is a different product, and we would rather tell you now than waste your time.

items.label: Next step
items.value: Send one page you generated. The edit comes back with a note on what changed and why.

data.title: What the edit covers
data.subtitle: Every pass does all six. We do not sell them separately because they do not work separately.

items.title: A position on the page
items.text: One claim the piece commits to, and it comes from you, so we ask when we do not have it.

items.title: Structure an engine can lift
items.text: The answer at the top of each section, self-contained passages, and headings that track the question somebody asked.

items.title: Claims get checked
items.text: Generated content states things with confidence whether or not they are true, so anything checkable gets checked.

items.title: Your voice on the page
items.text: We read your published work first and edit toward how you already sound, so the library holds together.

items.title: A title that tracks the question
items.text: Headline and meta rewritten toward the question somebody types.

items.title: A read across the library
items.text: We check the page against the rest of your site so you stop publishing one argument several times over, with every version chasing the same query.

data.title: What the edit is fixing
data.subtitle: The problems in generated content are rarely errors. That is what makes them hard to see.

items.title: It has no position
items.text: A model produces the balanced summary of what has been thought, because it has nothing at stake in being wrong, and editing puts a claim on the page that somebody would argue with.

items.title: It is new to you and to nobody else
items.text: You had not seen that output before, so it read as something new, and it came from everyone, which is why citation goes somewhere else.

items.title: It hedges where it needs to commit
items.text: Can help you. May improve. Often considered. An engine cannot attribute a claim you never made, so the hedges get replaced with something you will stand behind.

items.title: It carries the tells
items.text: The two-beat reversal, the sentence that announces its own importance, the inflated descriptor standing in for a name. Readers who see enough of these recognize the shape.

data.title: What changes when a person edits it
data.subtitle: The page looks about the same, and what it does changes.

items.title: It becomes quotable
items.text: Self-contained passages that hold up when an engine lifts one off the page, which is the shape that gets cited.

items.title: It sounds like you
items.text: Edited toward the voice already on your site, so the page sounds like the rest of what you publish.

items.title: It says something checkable
items.text: Claims with support attached, so a reader has a reason to believe it and an engine has something to attribute.

items.title: It stops competing with itself
items.text: A library edited as a set stops repeating one argument across page after page, each one chasing the same query.

data.title: How the editing works
data.subtitle: Four steps, and you are involved in the second one.

steps.title: Send us what you generated
steps.text: One page or a library. We read what you already publish alongside it so the edit moves toward your voice rather than ours.

steps.title: We ask you what you think
steps.text: Every piece needs one position, and the position has to be yours, so we ask a short question and write your answer into the page.

steps.title: An editor rewrites it
steps.text: Position, structure, claims, voice. The same pass every time, done by a person who writes for a living.

steps.title: You get it back with the reasoning
steps.text: The edited page plus what changed and why, so your team learns the pattern instead of sending us the same problem next month.

items.question: Is this a tool or a service?
items.answer: A service. People do the editing. If you are looking for software that cleans up AI prose automatically, this is the wrong page and we would rather say so than sell you something else.

items.question: Do you use AI in the editing?
items.answer: For research and checking, yes. For the writing, no. Looking backward through what already exists is what a model is good at, and that is where we point it.

items.question: Why can a model not edit its own output?
items.answer: It can fix grammar and tighten sentences, and it cannot supply a position it does not hold or a detail it has never encountered, which are the two things missing from the draft.

items.question: What if we do not have a strong opinion on the topic?
items.answer: Then we ask questions until one turns up. In our experience the opinion is usually there and has never been written down, which is a different problem from not having one.

items.question: Can you edit at volume?
items.answer: Yes, and we will tell you if volume is the wrong answer for your situation, because fewer pages that say something tend to outperform a big library that says nothing.

items.question: How do we start?
items.answer: Send one page you generated. There is nothing to sign before you see the edit.
